fran: quick sync: we need a decision on per-head vs per-tensor quant for fp8 rollout. ops saw headwise instability on several longconv logs. thoughts?
ivy: headwise gives better accuracy in many cases but it's noisier for tiny batches. per-tensor is cheaper and more stable. tradeoff depends on workload shape.
tom: true. our runtime currently assumes per-channel stats available; switching to per-tensor at load time is cheap but loses quality for some models. we should expose a deploy-time contract: profile declares supported modes and runtime picks best.
fran: proposal: profile metadata includes `supported_precision_modes: ["per_head","per_tensor"]` and `default_mode`. runtime does auto-selection: prefer per_head when batch>=4 and cv(scale)<=0.2 else fall back to per_tensor.
ivy: prefer adding a safety override: `precision_preference` in model config with values `auto|prefer_head|prefer_tensor` so platform teams can pin behavior for sensitive customers.
tom: need to define the detection heuristics precisely. propose: compute per-channel scale vector; if coeff_var(scale) < 0.2 and kurtosis < 3 -> per_head safe. else per_tensor.
fran: where lives this logic? in loader or hot path? loader is better for compute cost but lacks request-level batch info. hot path has batch info but must be cheap. compromise: loader hints with `head_safe_hint` and runtime validates per-request; if mismatch runtime uses fast fallback.
ivy: agree. also important: KV-cache provenance must carry `precision_mode` so cached activations encoded with per_head aren't applied when runtime uses per_tensor. otherwise subtle bias.
tom: add small 8B header to KV entries: 1b mode enum + 3b profile hash + 4b scale_ver. cheap.
fran: telemetry and regression criteria: measure seeded eval top1 and degeneration score. Canary fails if top1 drops >1% or degscore increases >2 points for a cohort. Also track cost delta per-caller.
ivy: need E2E bench: synthesize three cohorts: conversational longctx, shortburst single-shot, and embeddings-ish transformer calls. Run with head, tensor, and auto modes.
tom: add unit test: replay shadow logs where mode flips mid-conversation; assert no >0.5% token shift and no kv.profile_mismatch >0.01%.
fran: rollout plan: 1) profile metadata spec + KV header, 2) runtime heuristics + fast-path fallback, 3) opt-in admin flag `force_precision_mode` for tenants, 4) 2-week shadow canary with 5% traffic, dashboards.
ops-bot: deploy-note: quant-mode-selector v1 rolled to shadow with tag `quant.mode.auto=true` at 14:22 UTC. PR template: https://git.redwood/infra/quant-mode-selector.
ivy: action items: fran -> spec + docs; tom -> KV header + runtime fast check; ivy -> bench harness + telem dashboards. Target PRs today, shadow for 14 days.
fran: snippet for runtime check: ```py
scales = compute_channel_scales(tensor)
cv = np.std(scales)/np.mean(scales)
if batch_size >= 4 and cv <= 0.2 and kurtosis(scales) <= 3:
  use_mode('per_head')
else:
  use_mode('per_tensor')
```
tom: note: if mode changes mid-seq, evict kv entries with mismatched header. set evict threshold to 0.01% mismatch over 5m.
ivy: keeping cost in mind: per_head increases bandwidth and compute. we'll gate broad rollout until cost dashboard shows <8% token-cost delta for target customers.
fran: ok let's do this. will open PR + attach bench traces. will ping channel when canary starts reporting. :thumbsup:
